messages:
kevin_h: seeing intermittent timeouts + full hangs on multi-node TP jobs after the kernel-selector and batch-heuristic change we rolled yesterday. 2/8 jobs succeed, others hit long NCCL stalls then timeout. Anyone seen this pattern?
maria_s: thanks for flagging. which clusters, commit hash?
kevin_h: dedicated-pool-2 (eu), commit a7f3d9b (kernel-selector: prefer_fused_kernels=true, batch-heuristic: dynamic_prefix_grouping). start ts 1781234500.
tom_k: can you paste the tail of the worker logs where it stalls? NCCL timeouts usually show up as repeated "watchdog" messages.
kevin_h: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] INFO TP-rank-3: step 214 enter allreduce
[2026-03-18 14:02:11] WARN NCCL: op allreduce req=0x7f8a9... waiting for partner
[2026-03-18 14:02:35] ERROR TP-rank-3: allreduce watchdog timeout after 24000ms
[2026-03-18 14:02:35] INFO TP-rank-3: attempting rendezvous retry (attempt=1)
[2026-03-18 14:03:05] INFO TP-rank-3: aborting job: timeout
```

kevin_h: profiler snapshot shows heavy imbalance on comm vs compute:
```
step 214: compute 90ms, allreduce 1150ms, overlap 5ms
step 215: compute 88ms, allreduce 1200ms, overlap 3ms
```

maria_s: that allreduce number is huge. good to confirm it's multi-node (not just intra-node NCCL).
kevin_h: yes 4 nodes, tensor-parallel shards across nodes.
runtime-ci: auto-run of nccl check on affected node pool produced intermittent ranks failing to establish peer connections (see run 2026-03-18T14:00Z).
infra-bot: created incident INC-2026-104: multi-node TP allreduce stalls in dedicated-pool-2. Paging on-call.

olga_r: quick hypothesis: the kernel-selector fused kernels change increased per-GPU compute microbursts, which can starve RNIC progress or trigger NCCL progress anomalies when comm/compute overlap is poor. also dynamic batching can fragment KV cache updates causing uneven step timing.

maria_s: agree. we recently removed async-progress workaround in the kernel path to avoid extra CPU threads. that could reduce NCCL progress scheduling.

tom_k: can we repro with perf traces? run the lightweight profiler w/ NCCL tracing and host-side timeline. command: `./tools/profiler --job tp --nodes 4 --nccl-trace --host-timeline --workload small`

kevin_h: kicked it off. attaching condensed trace snippets:
```
[timeline] rank0: compute kernel 0-60ms, kernel 2 200-260ms, host>ncclAllReduce start 260ms
[timeline] rank1: compute kernel 0-180ms, host>ncclAllReduce start 180ms
```

kevin_h: basically ranks enter allreduce at very different times -> long warm waits.

olga_r: that smells like batching heuristic creating variable sequence lengths / KV cache misses; some ranks doing cache fetches leading to 2-3x extra compute before rendezvous.

maria_s: suggested short-term mitigation: pin kernel-selector to previous commit and disable dynamic_prefix_grouping. can we patch the rollout?

tom_k: yes, we can hotfix the config on dedicated-pool-2 and restart the pool. doing canary with 2 jobs first.

kevin_h: started canary restart at 14:25Z.

runtime-ci: canary results: 2/2 jobs pass under pinned config.

kevin_h: after rollback, profiler shows resumed overlap:
```
step 320: compute 95ms, allreduce 130ms, overlap 80ms
step 321: compute 92ms, allreduce 125ms, overlap 75ms
```

maria_s: good sign. next: we should add a microbenchmark in CI that exercises fused vs unfused kernels under realistic KV cache miss rates and multi-node TP layout. add NCCL trace assertion to detect >300ms allreduce on 4-node TP jobs.

olga_r: also re-enable async-progress thread temporarily in kernel path as an experiment — measure CPU cost vs reduced NCCL stalls.

tom_k: filed perf ticket PERF-742 with reproducer and trace. we should also add a batching invariant: max per-rank extra compute due to prefix grouping <= 30ms.

kevin_h: leaving logs for postmortem. thanks all. will monitor INC-2026-104 and update. :thumbsup:

maria_s: great triage. pls add notes to postmortem and link kernel-selector PR a7f3d9b for rollback rationale.

kevin_h: done. added notes and traces to the incident doc. last check-in at 14:37Z, system stable.

infra-bot: INC-2026-104 moved to resolved - mitigated by rollback and config change.
